The UC Irvine Langson Orange County Museum of Art seeks a detail-oriented and highly organized museum professional to serve as Exhibitions and Publications Manager. Reporting to the Senior Director of Collections and Exhibitions Management, this position independently manages project coordination and implementation across the museum's exhibitions and publications programs. The Exhibitions and Publications Manager plays a key role in keeping complex, multi-stakeholder projects on track by maintaining schedules, monitoring budgets, coordinating agreements, identifying and resolving project issues, and tracking deliverables throughout the full project lifecycle. This position works closely with curatorial, registration, design, education, communications, and external partners, and is well-suited for an experienced museum professional with demonstrated project management experience and the ability to drive complex, multi-stakeholder projects to completion independently.
Demonstrated expertise in either museum exhibitions coordination or publications production, with an interest in developing proficiency across both areas.
Proficiency in project management platforms such as Asana, Basecamp, Smartsheet, or comparable tools.
Proficiency in spreadsheet software, project tracking tools, and standard office applications. Working knowledge of common organization- or research-specific and other computer application programs.
Familiarity with museum collections management systems and loan documentation processes.
Proficient in communication and interpersonal skills to communicate effectively, both verbally and in writing with a range of internal and external partners.
Proficient in ability to use discretion and maintain all confidentiality.
Demonstrates ability to use sound judgment in responding to issues and concerns.

Exceptional organizational skills and attention to detail, with a strong commitment to accuracy, follow-through, and maintaining thorough records. Demonstrates ability to analyze, research and synthesize large amounts of data.
Working knowledge of applicable policy analysis techniques.
